Interview Demo
Internal tools CMS 2022

Internal App
Review System

A ground-up rebuild of Wix App Market's internal review platform, after the review team had abandoned it for spreadsheets and Google Docs.

Background

The problem

Wix App Market's internal review platform is the tool Account Managers use to evaluate and approve apps before they go live, spanning four interconnected product areas.

When I joined, the team had stopped using it. Review work was scattered across personal Google Docs, with no shared history, no visibility between submissions, and no consistent handoffs. The cycle below shows what the process actually looked like.

App review cycle

Previously: review work happened across Google Docs, Sheets, and Slides with no shared history

Process
Research

Research

Met with Account Managers to walk through the current system, shadowed them running actual reviews, audited the Docs and Sheets they were using instead, and pulled analytics on time to publish and how many resubmissions an app typically needed. That surfaced:

  • Confusing UI in the current system
  • Difficulty writing a consistent review
  • Weak information architecture
  • No integrated workflow
Process
Scope

Deciding on scope

Before designing any screens, I mapped the product into four areas, building on Wix's own UI system to fix the confusing-UI complaint at the platform level first.

① App directory and queue
Browse, filter, and assign every app across all review stages. A structural makeover to fix the weak information architecture.
② App page
One app's full history, team, and status in a single view. Closed the no-integrated-workflow gap.
③ Review workspace
Built from scratch to replace ad-hoc Google Doc reviews
④ Team management
Role-based access and reviewer assignments across the team

Impact

Impact

The tool is still actively used by Wix's Developer Relations team, and became their primary review surface. It reduced account manager workload, shortened the review cycle, and made app evaluations faster and more consistent across the team.

The team had already voted with their feet, doing the actual review work in spreadsheets outside the platform. Success wasn't launching a redesign; it was building something good enough that they'd stop reaching for Google Docs. The tool became their primary review surface, which is the only metric that actually mattered.
